decision: Force the headless OpenCV 4.x wheel on every platform in tools/venv.sh, and assert cv2.__version__ starts with 4.
why: rapidocr pulls an unpinned opencv-python that wins the cv2 import over homr's pinned headless <5; the swap existed but was guarded by uname = Linux.
evidence: venv held opencv-python 5.0.0.93 and opencv-python-headless 4.14.0.94 at once.
result: Applied. cv2 is now 4.14.0 and rapidocr still imports.

decision: Do not re-dump the golden fixtures.
why: OpenCV 4.14.0 and 5.0.0 agree on minAreaRect and boxPoints, and the checked-in boxes-*.json reproduce byte for byte under 4.14.0 including the -45 entries.
evidence: Raw minAreaRect and boxPoints on boxes-stems_rest idx 0 and 96 matched the stored box and polygon exactly.
result: Fixtures kept. 42 files untouched.

decision: Convert every raw opencv.js rect to opencv-python's [-90, 0) convention before homr's normalisation, by subtracting 90 and swapping w/h while the angle is >= 0.
why: opencv.js 4.12.0 uses the post-4.5.1 (0, 90] convention; opencv-python 4.14.0 uses the pre-4.5.1 one. Normalisation absorbs the difference everywhere except exactly +-45, where homr's comparisons are strict.
evidence: 86 of 717 rotated-box entries disagreed in angle sign before the conversion and 0 after; bar_lines went to 103/103 exact on both rect and polygon.
result: Adopted as the design.

decision: Widen the golden box tolerance to cover the angle at 1e-3, not just centres and sizes.
why: Python stores the rect as float32 and the port recomputes in float64.
evidence: Worst observed angle delta 7.7e-7, worst centre/size delta 2.4e-4 across 967 entries.
result: testing.md needs the note; cause identified as required.

decision: Accept that box polygons are not bit-exact, and measure rather than tolerate.
why: The rect differs by ~1e-4 between the two builds, which flips a corner across an integer boundary.
evidence: 18 of 967 entries differ by one pixel on one corner. trunc, floor and an fround pass score identically; round scores worse; a hand-rolled float32 boxPoints matched 0 of 967.
result: Use cv.boxPoints on the converted rect. Downstream merge risk recorded, resolvable only once the merge runs.

decision: Build noteheads through minAreaRect over the concatenated contours, not fitEllipse.
why: _get_ellipse_for_whole_group refits with minAreaRect and every box reaches it, singleton groups included; fitEllipse only gates the 5-point minimum and shapes the polygon the overlap test reads.
evidence: Per-entry fitEllipse diverged in the centre; the minAreaRect route gave 81/81 at 2.4e-4 with no angle mismatch.
result: Adopted.

decision: Scope phase 4 to the five predict_symbols box lists plus prepare_bar_line_image, and leave staff_fragments-broken to phase 5.
why: break_wide_fragments is staff_detection.py, a phase-5 module; the five lists are reproducible from the dumped mask-filtered-*.png alone.
evidence: dump-golden.py writes mask-filtered-* after filter_predictions and make_lines_stronger, so no phase-5 code is needed for the five.
result: Adopted. brace_dot testable but empty on this page.

decision: Do not convert a fitEllipse rect; convert only minAreaRect.
why: The two producers sit in different conventions. fitEllipse agrees bit for bit across opencv.js 4.12.0 and opencv-python 4.14.0; minAreaRect does not.
evidence: 81 of 81 noteheads, worst delta exactly 0 on centre, size and angle. Angle range 10.761 to 67.928, consistent with [0,180) in both.
result: Fork 1 resolved: two producer-specific brands, not one raw-rect type.

decision: Correction: both max_size filters use or, and the real asymmetry is the > 0 per-dimension guard, present on boxes and absent on ellipses.
why: An earlier version of the findings document said the ellipse filter used and. Read from source lines 360-440.
evidence: create_bounding_ellipses has no > 0 guard, so max_size=(100,-1) would reject every ellipse rather than disable the height check.
result: Findings document corrected. Candidate B found this.

decision: Correction: there is a sixth call shape, brace_dot with max_size=(100,-1), and it is the only one exercising the disable rule.
why: The findings document claimed five call shapes and that the rule might be trimmed.
evidence: main.py:280 / dump-golden.py:187.
result: Findings document corrected. Candidate A found this.

decision: No runtime range check on toLegacyAngleConvention; the two producer brands are the whole guard.
why: The while-loop is total: an angle already in [-90, 0) makes zero iterations and passes through unchanged, so a range check would refuse a correct pre-4.5.1 result rather than catch a mislabel. Candidate A wanted the check because its legacyRectOf took the producer as a string argument, which the brands replace.
evidence: Probed @techstark/opencv-js 4.12.0 directly: minAreaRect on a 20x10 axis-aligned contour answers angle +90, size (10, 20), which the loop turns into -90 with the size unchanged, matching what the findings record for opencv-python.
result: Applied. The brands make a wrong conversion a compile error; no throw exists.

decision: axisBoxOf narrows from RotatedBox | Ellipse to RotatedBox.
why: to_bounding_box is defined on RotatedBoundingBox, not on AngledBoundingBox, so no Ellipse ever reaches it in homr. Phase 1's wider signature let one.
evidence: bounding_boxes.py lines 299-309; grep found the method on no other class.
result: Applied. Candidate B's finding about already-shipped code.

decision: Phase 4's new modules take kebab-case filenames (mat-plane.ts, box-merge.ts, ...), not the camelCase the design packages wrote.
why: biome's useFilenamingConvention is an error in this repo and both candidate designs named files in camelCase, so their literal names do not pass npm run lint.
evidence: npx biome check refused src/cv/matPlane.ts and matPoints.ts by name; the existing tree is all kebab-case (default-source.ts).
result: Applied. src/cv/boxes.ts also became src/cv/create-boxes.ts, so no two modules share the basename boxes.ts.

decision: UnionFind stays private to box-merge.ts; mergeOverlappingGroups takes items and a predicate, not groups.
why: Python's groups list is never mutated, so _do_groups_overlap always compares the original singletons and reduces to one predicate call per pair. Exporting the union-find would be a second surface with no caller.
evidence: The non-ascending-root case is reachable through the predicate alone, so nothing needs a hand-made union sequence to pin the Map contract.
result: Applied. Candidate B's collapse, and the module imports no cv.

decision: OverlapTester.overlaps / .overlapsAny replace free isOverlapping / isOverlappingWithAny functions rather than sitting beside them.
why: The synthesis takes the tester from candidate A, and it is the same relation: a second one-shot pair would be two names for one behaviour with no caller until phase 5, and the one-shot is the shape A measured as unusable in the merge.
evidence: Candidate A measured roughly 75 000 Mat allocations per page for the one-Mat-per-comparison form; the test asserts 4 keeps across 6 comparisons.
result: Applied. Phase 5 constructs a tester per loop, which is the shape it wants anyway.

decision: Use homr's own names for the per-box operations (makeBoxThicker, makeBoxTaller, ...) rather than the synthesis's prose names (thicker, taller).
why: Fork 3 settles the *typing* -- kind-preserving through a generic, kind-collapsing by return type -- and fork 2 puts the module in candidate B's map, whose whole naming convention mirrors the Python. createRotatedBoundingBoxes, doPolygonsOverlap and predictSymbols all read that way, so one file naming differently would be the odd one out.
evidence: No measurement; a naming call, recorded because the synthesis writes the other names.
result: Applied.

decision: makeBoxThicker keeps RotatedBoundingBox's `thickness <= 0` early return for ellipses too, which BoundingEllipse does not have.
why: The ellipse override has no guard, so a non-positive thickness there rebuilds the polygon from the normalised rect instead of leaving it alone -- a real difference, but unreachable: the three call sites pass 15, 30 and a positive tolerance, and thicken_boxes is never given a value.
evidence: grep of the whole homr package for make_box_thicker: note_detection.py:131 (15), brace_dot_detection.py:53/72/91, bounding_boxes.py:385 (thicken_boxes, never passed).
result: Applied, with the asymmetry named in the doc comment. Branching on kind would reintroduce the isinstance chain fork 3 removes, for dead code.

decision: No toBoundingBox alias beside axisBoxOf.
why: Candidate B proposed one so the exported name matches Python's, but every other name in the phase is already the camelCase equivalent rather than a transliteration, and axisBoxOf shipped in phase 1.
evidence: None needed; it is one name for one function either way.
result: Not applied.

decision: polygonViaBoxPoints takes no MatScope, where candidate B's sketch does.
why: cv.boxPoints hands back a plain JavaScript array of {x, y} and allocates no Mat, so a scope parameter would be a lie about what the function owns. Candidate A's sketch already had it right.
evidence: Probed directly on 4.12.0: boxPoints accepts a plain rect literal and returns Array.isArray === true with no delete().
result: Applied. polygonViaEllipse2Poly does take one, because its seventh argument must be a PointVector.

decision: Correction: reimplement boxPoints in float32 from OpenCV's direct four-corner formula instead of calling cv.boxPoints, reversing the 2026-09-28 row above.
why: opencv.js 4.12.0's boxPoints reflects the third and fourth corners through the centre where opencv-python 4.14.0 derives all four, so on a bit-identical rect the reflection lands on an integer that the direct form lands 3e-5 below and int() differs by one. Three staff_fragments entries hit it with a bit-exact stored rect, which the synthesis's fork 4 tolerance cannot admit and must not be widened to.
evidence: Over the 595 of 634 rotated golden entries whose raw minAreaRect is bit-identical between the builds: cv.boxPoints equals the reflecting formula 595/595, the direct formula equals opencv-python's floats 595/595, cv.boxPoints equals opencv-python's floats 591/595.
result: Applied. staff_fragments goes 144 to 147 of 147 polygons exact and fork 4 stays as settled. boxPoints left REQUIRED_MEMBERS; the earlier row's "matched 0 of 967" is retracted in phase-4-findings.md.

decision: Drop candidate A's FittedShape wrapper and its float outline; the fitters return plain RotatedBox[] and Ellipse[].
why: It existed only to carry the pre-truncation float so the golden test could derive a per-box corner bound. The synthesis's fork 4 dropped that bound, and the direct boxPoints formula removes the last case that needed one, so the wrapper and shapesOf would be a parameter with no reader.
evidence: Every polygon of the five lists is now exact but one, whose rect is inexact, so the rect-conditioned rule is sufficient.
result: Applied.

decision: predictSymbols takes SegmentationMasks, not InputPredictions.
why: predict_symbols reads only the five masks off its InputPredictions; taking the whole thing would be a parameter the function never looks at.
result: Applied. Candidate B's signature.
